newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Summit says tests confirm gold at Carrick.
newsitem.headline: Summit says tests confirm gold at Carrick.

text.p: Listed mining company Summit Gold NL said on Friday that a second phase of soil sampling had confirmed the presence of gold at the Carrick Goldfield in Central Otago in New Zealand's South Island.

"The infill sampling, when combined with the previously reported soil results, clearly defines a strong coincident gold arsenic hanging wall anomaly averaging 150 metres wide and a second narrow 20 to 40 metre wide footwall zone to the west," Summit said in a statement to the New Zealand Stock Exchange.

The sampling showed gold values up to 2.75 grams per tonne in the zones which extend for over two kilometres. The identified zones were masked by alluvial cover and old sluicings to the north and remain open to the south, the company said.
The new soil data was being integrated with structural mapping and topographic information and the company was planning a drilling programme designed to test the hanging wall zone.
Percussion drilling was scheduled to start at Carrick in the first quarter of 1997.
Summit first reported finding traces of gold at Carrick in mid-December. Its share price spiked up sharply to a peak of 85 NZ cents after the first report before easing back to 60 cents.
Following Friday's announcement it was up seven cents on Thurday's close at 61 cents in early trading. A year ago the share price was around seven cents.
